# Input Data

## Packages

::: callout-note
I used the `changepoint` package to test for a change in mean in the data set. The `cpt.mean()` package tested this using the AMOC method, which was suitable for data with a single change point.
:::
```{r}
library(tidyverse)
if(require("changepoint")){
    print("lme4 is loaded correctly")
} else {
    print("trying to install changepoint")
    install.packages("changepoint")
    if(require(changepoint)){
        print("changepoint installed and loaded")
    } else {
        stop("could not install changepoint")
    }
}
```

## Plot Data
```{r}
#| output: false
files <-list.files(path="../plots/data",full.names=T)
df <- files |> map_dfr(read_csv) 
```


## Picture details



```{r}
#| output: false

pic_details <- read_csv("../plots/picture_details.csv") |> 
  rename(picid = lineup_id) |> 
  select(picid,theta,cpLoc,sigma,version)
```


# Change Point Analysis

::: callout-note
Only analyzed target plots.
:::

```{r}
#| warning: false

cploc_CPD <- function(x){
  cpt.mean(x, method="AMOC",class=FALSE)->cploc # <1>
  cploc
}

mean_diff <- function(x){
  cpt.mean(x, method="AMOC",class=TRUE)->cploc 
  param.est(cploc)$mean |> diff() |> as.numeric()
}
cp_test_results <- df |> 
  filter(panel=="target") |>
  group_by(picid) |> 
  summarize(change_point = cploc_CPD(value)[1],
            confvalue = cploc_CPD(value)[2] |> round(4),
            shift_size = mean_diff(value) |> round(1)) |> 
  mutate(CP_detected = case_when(change_point==30 | confvalue <0.90~"No", # <2>
                                 .default="Yes")) |> # <2> 
ungroup()

cp_test_results |> left_join(pic_details,by="picid") |>  #<3>
  mutate(visual_changepoint = round(30*cpLoc,2)) |> 
  relocate(visual_changepoint,.before=change_point) |> 
  relocate(shift_size,.before= theta) -> cp_test_results

cp_test_results |>  
DT::datatable()
```


1. Outputs a vector with length 2: estimated change point location and "confidence value". 

2. If the change point is set at 30, this means there was no detected change point. If the confidence value < 0.90 when the change point is less than 30, this means the algorithm is not too sure that we have a change point.

3. Joining the target plot distribution details with the change point results.

:::callout-warning
Confidence value is not the same as the confidence level in a confidence level interval. It's basically telling us if the algorithm is sure that there is indeed a change point there.
:::


## Confidence Value Plots

```{r}
confvalue_plt <- cp_test_results |> 
mutate(Location=case_when(visual_changepoint == 10~"Early",
                visual_changepoint == 15~"Middle",
                visual_changepoint == 20~"Late"),
MagDir = case_when(theta ==-5 ~"- High Shift", theta ==5 ~"+ High Shift", theta==3~ "+ Medium Shift", theta==-3~ "- Medium Shift", theta == 1~" + Low", theta == - 1~" - Low"),
Variance = case_when(sigma==1~"Low",sigma==2~"High")) |> 
mutate(MagDir = factor(MagDir, levels=c("- High Shift","- Medium Shift"," - Low"," + Low","+ Medium Shift","+ High Shift")),
Variance = factor(Variance,levels=c("Low","High")),
Location = factor(Location,levels=c("Early","Middle","Late"))) |> 
dplyr::select(confvalue,CP_detected,Location,MagDir,Variance)

confvalue_plt |> ggplot(aes(y=MagDir,x=confvalue)) + facet_grid(Location~ Variance) + geom_bar(stat="identity") + theme_bw()
```

::: callout-warning
I don't know why the confidence value is peaking at 2! It's supposed to all be below 1.
:::
